topicData.topic: Why large enterprises have 'blocked agency' — skilled workers trapped in organizations that aren't built to let them use AI the way they've learned to
topicData.angle: Your best people have figured out how to work with AI. Your systems haven't figured out how to let them.

postText:
10% of workers are what the Microsoft Work Trend Index calls "blocked agency."

High individual AI skill. Low organizational readiness.

These aren't your laggards. These are the people who rebuilt their own workflows without being asked. Who figured out how to use agents for multi-step work while the rest of the business was still running AI awareness sessions.

And they're stuck.

Not because they lack ability. Because the metrics, incentives, and approval structures around them were designed for a completely different way of working.

I have watched this exact pattern play out in a telecoms company with 28,000 employees. The people who move fastest hit the hardest walls. The system doesn't reward reinvention — it rewards delivery against targets that were set before any of this existed.

You spent years developing that talent. And then without meaning to, you built a cage around it.

That is not an AI capability problem. It is a leadership design problem.

Where are you seeing this show up first in your organisation?

#EnterpriseAI #DigitalTransformation #TechLeadership
